title: candidate-feedback-draft-samir-patel-2026-03-06
content:
Candidate: Samir Patel
Role: Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime (IC4/IC5 TBD)
Interview date: 2026-03-05
Interviewers: Lena M. (system design), Omar H. (coding/perf), Priya D. (behavioural/ops)

Quick summary:
- Strong systems intuition, good at tradeoffs for latency vs cost.
- Solid CS fundamentals; coding was correct but a bit rough on edge cases and tests.
- Practical experience building inference infra at scale (prefix/KV cache, sharding, batching) but less hands-on with CUDA kernels.
- Good communicator, clear thinking under pressure, gravitates to reliability-related concerns.

Scorecard (1-5):
- Technical (algorithms/data structures): 4
- System design & architecture: 4.5
- Performance/optimizations (latency/cost): 4
- Low-level HW/CUDA experience: 2.5
- Product/operational sense: 4
- Communication & collaboration: 4
- Culture fit (Redwood values): 4
- Overall recommendation: Strong hire / hire with minor leveling caveat (may be IC4 with growth path to IC5)

Detailed notes:
- System design (Lena):
  - Proposed a practical multi-tenant runtime design with routing by SLA and prefix caching.
  - Liked the KV-cache eviction policy tradeoff he sketched (LRU + recency-weighted sampling) and how he handled consistency/per-tenant isolation.
  - Mentioned async batching and warm-starting KV contexts; good awareness of tail latency pitfalls.
  - Follow-ups: ask for more detail on rollout strategy for model-variant fallbacks (how to test fallback correctness, canary rollout plan).

- Coding / perf (Omar):
  - 45-min live coding on a streaming aggregator problem. Correct approach (incremental buffering), passed main cases. Missed a couple edge cases (off-by-one in windowing) but fixed after prompt.
  - Talked through memory/perf tradeoffs and gave a plausible O(n) / O(1) space variant.
  - Discussion on quantization: knows high-level impact (INT8 tradeoffs) but not experienced in building quantized kernels.
  - Can ramp on lower-level perf work with mentorship; stronger on infra + orchestration than CUDA kernel dev.

- Behavioral / ops (Priya):
  - Examples of incident ownership, postmortem culture. Clear on on-call practices, runbooks, where to draw the line on automation vs manual recovery.
  - Good coaching examples: mentored two juniors to ship performance improvements.

Risks / concerns:
- Limited hands-on GPU/kernel dev experience. If we need someone to tune kernels or write CUDA it would be a gap.
- Slight roughness in coding hygiene (tests/edge-case thinking) — likely fixable in a couple months with code reviews and pairing.

Compensation/leveling notes:
- Current comp expectation given was in line with IC4-IC5 range; recommend offering at IC4 with explicit growth plan to IC5 after 6-12 months based on impact (ownership of a major runtime feature, e.g., autoscaling policy + caching improvements).

Next steps suggested:
- Check references (2 managers, 1 peer) focusing on low-level perf work and how he ramped on unfamiliar tech (CUDA or other HW-specific work).
- Short follow-up with senior infra engineer (maybe someone from runtime or release-engineering) to validate kernel/quantization ramp plan — 30m deep dive.
- Draft verbal offer for IC4 with manager approval pending reference feedback.

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Add specific follow-up question list for reference check (see linked doc draft)
- Put candidate in "offer pipeline" Slack thread and tag hiring manager (Lena)
- If manager prefers stronger kernel experience, consider keeping in "strong candidate but not fit" bin for kernel-specialist req.

Links & artifacts: JIRA-7654 (req), confluence page draft linked above, coding exercise (attached in GH pr/4321).

Misc rough thoughts (brain dump):
- Could pair Samir with a senior infra person for first 3 months to cover CUDA gaps; lots of value in his system-level thinking for our routing/caching work.
- Potential quick win: put him on the batching/caching ownership to reduce per-token cost by 10-15% in Q3.
- Keep level flexible; if he demonstrates quick kernel ramp (30-60 days) we can accelerate to IC5.

-- Michael
